record.title: HGM-Dual reports more accurate long-horizon planning harnesses under a fixed evaluation budget
record.summary: HGM-Dual is a harness-search method that summarizes the effects of earlier edits along a lineage and uses observed constraint failures to generate targeted alternatives alongside a general edit. In author-reported DeepPlanning travel and shopping evaluations, it improves case accuracy over a customized HGM baseline at 4,000 plan evaluations; on shopping it exceeds that baseline’s 4,000-evaluation result with 1,000 evaluations. These are results on two constrained tasks with fixed model choices. Appendix API costs cover task-agent evaluations and depend on cache assumptions; they do not establish total optimization cost or general planning capability.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: HGM-Dual augments evolutionary harness search with structured records of edits and their outcomes along a parent lineage, and generates both a general child and error-conditioned children when diagnostic-stability gates are met. The paper leaves the underlying language-model weights fixed.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On DeepPlanning travel and shopping tasks, the authors report that at a 4,000-plan evaluation budget HGM-Dual exceeds the strongest HGM-CF baseline in case accuracy: 64.38% versus 56.25% on travel and 66.67% versus 60.83% on shopping. These are author-reported results on two constrained tasks, not an independent reproduction or general planning-capability result.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: At 1,000 plan evaluations, the authors report a 70.83% shopping case-accuracy result for HGM-Dual, exceeding HGM-CF's 60.83% result at 4,000 evaluations. The paper estimates task-agent API use for 1,000 sample evaluations at $140–$1,010 depending on task and prompt-cache assumptions; these estimates exclude the editor's optimization cost and are not measured total-dollar savings.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The study does not establish that the reported gains transfer beyond the two DeepPlanning tasks, persist across model choices or prospective benchmarks, or reduce total optimization cost in dollars.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of HGM-Dual's reported results or analysis was inspected.
The study evaluates only travel and shopping tasks from DeepPlanning; prospective transfer to other constrained planning environments is unknown.
The appendix estimates task-agent API evaluation cost under prompt-cache assumptions but does not give a complete measured dollar cost including editor calls and search overhead.

brief.importance_rationale: If the author-reported results hold, lineage-aware edit attribution and failure-targeted harness search could change optimization choices for long-horizon planning agents. The evidence covers only travel and shopping tasks, and evaluation-count efficiency is not a general monetary-cost or capability result.
limitations: The evaluation covers two constrained DeepPlanning tasks, travel and shopping; transfer to other planning domains is unestablished.

The main setup uses fixed GPT-5.4 editor and GPT-5.4-mini task-agent models. The additional Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B task-agent test reports higher composite score but little case-accuracy change; it does not establish broad model transfer.
Task-agent API cost values are estimates for sample evaluations under stated prompt-cache assumptions, not measured total optimization cost or realized savings.
All performance results are reported by the paper's authors; no independent reproduction was performed in this review.
brief.summary: HGM-Dual is a harness-search method that summarizes the effects of earlier edits along a lineage and uses observed constraint failures to generate targeted alternatives alongside a general edit. In author-reported DeepPlanning travel and shopping evaluations, it improves case accuracy over a customized HGM baseline at 4,000 plan evaluations; on shopping it exceeds that baseline’s 4,000-evaluation result with 1,000 evaluations. These are results on two constrained tasks with fixed model choices. Appendix API costs cover task-agent evaluations and depend on cache assumptions; they do not establish total optimization cost or general planning capability.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report that HGM-Dual improves travel and shopping case accuracy over HGM-CF at 4,000 plan evaluations: 64.38% versus 56.25% on travel and 66.67% versus 60.83% on shopping. At 1,000 evaluations, its shopping case accuracy is reported as 70.83%, compared with HGM-CF's final 60.83% at 4,000 evaluations.
technical.compute_or_cost: The paper estimates task-agent API cost for 1,000 sample evaluations at $140–$1,010 across task and optimization conditions. Bounds assume about 80% input-token prompt caching versus no caching. This is estimated task-agent evaluation spend, not total optimization cost; editor calls and other costs are not represented by these figures.
technical.demonstrated_result: The arXiv preprint documents the proposed method and author-reported DeepPlanning results. No independent reproduction was performed in this review; the performance claims remain CLAIMED.
technical.mechanism: HGM-Dual provides the editor with a structured summary of edits and their observed outcomes along an agent-harness lineage. It generates a general child and, when diagnostic stability gates pass, two children targeted to the parent harness's most frequent evaluator-defined errors; it retains the best child under the optimization score.
technical.regime: The paper evaluates travel and shopping tasks from DeepPlanning. Unless otherwise specified, the editor is GPT-5.4 at medium reasoning effort and the task agent is GPT-5.4-mini at high effort. Each task uses 60 optimization samples and 120 evaluation samples, including 60 unseen samples. The reported search results use evaluation budgets up to 4,000 plans.
technical.reproducibility: This review inspected the full arXiv v1 HTML, including method, main results, ablations and cost appendix, but did not independently reproduce the results. The claims remain author-reported and are limited to the two stated tasks.
technical.strongest_baseline: The primary comparison is HGM-CF, a customized HGM variant given the same deterministic interface for task-agent code and logs. It is the strongest baseline on the four reported 4,000-evaluation metrics. The paper also compares ADAS, GEPA, vanilla HGM and HGM-CA, but evaluates ADAS and GEPA only at the 1,000-evaluation budget.

brief.title: HGM-Dual reports more accurate long-horizon planning harnesses under a fixed evaluation budget
brief.why_it_matters: Long-horizon planning agents can fail when one constraint violation invalidates an otherwise useful plan. If the reported results generalize, retaining edit-outcome history and targeting recurring failures may help harness search spend a limited evaluation budget more effectively. The current evidence comes from two planning tasks and does not establish broader transfer or total monetary savings.
